newsitem.title: UK: UK defence minister to meet troubled Gulf War vets.
newsitem.headline: UK defence minister to meet troubled Gulf War vets.

text.p: Britain's new Defence Minister George Robertson said on Wednesday he will meet Gulf War veterans and look into their claims to be suffering from so-called Gulf War Syndrome.
"We have an obligation to investigate sympathetically any illness suffered by those who have served their country," he said when announcing his plans for the ground-breaking talks on Thursday.
The Labour government, which won a landslide election victory on May 1, had already announced plans for more research and promised to improve the health care of veterans.
Officials also plan to extend research programmes into the causes of Gulf War Syndrome, including investigations into exposure to chemical weapons and organophosphate pesticides.

Veterans claim that evidence gathered in the United States support the theory that a "cocktail" of immunisations to protect them from chemical and biological warfare and pesticides may be responsible.
The ailments range from chronic fatigue and asthma to depression and skin ailments.
